gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Techtest.org's Michael Barton measured the S26 Ultra on a 5–11 V/5 A PPS charger (the 45 W 'Super Fast Charging 2.0' profile) and on a 5–21 V/5 A PPS charger (the 60 W profile). Both took about 1 h 02 min from 5% to 100%, with 49% vs 51% after 15 minutes. A charger without PPS, even a 100 W one, was capped at about 23 W.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited or ranked: GSMArena's lab tests (cited; 84% at 30 min, 43 min to full, and an unnamed third-party 67 W charger with similar times), ChargerLAB's EP-T6010 teardown (cited; 51.54 W), SamMobile's Trio article (cited; the Trio's PPS stops at 45 W), and Android Authority's test (60 W for about 2 min, about 48 W for about 16 min, 42 min to full). None of them puts the 60 W profile and the 45 W profile side by side to show how little the time to full changes. None gives the about-23 W ceiling for a charger without PPS. None names a third-party charger that a reviewer saw trigger Super Fast Charging 3.0. GSMArena's third-party charger has no model name, and ChatGPT said so.
decides: It confirms that PPS is the must-have and 20 V/3 A PPS is the nice-to-have. In Techtest's numbers, a charger without PPS is the real trap (about 23 W). The 45 W PPS tier lost only about 2 points of charge at 15 minutes and no time to full. That supports ranking third-party chargers whose PPS reaches 20–21 V at 3 A or more next to Samsung's EP-T6010 instead of treating Samsung's adapter as the only answer. Among the UGREEN chargers we link, the Nexode Air 65W is the only one a named reviewer has seen trigger Super Fast Charging 3.0 on an S26 Ultra. That was Forest Watch, in a UGREEN-sponsored article with no watt reading. Nobody has measured the Nexode 65W travel charger on the phone. Samsung's EP-T6010 stays the reference: it is the one charger whose S26 Ultra wattage a named lab measured (ChargerLAB, 51.54 W).

findings.label: Maplee-Tech: unbranded chargers on the S26 Ultra
findings.value: A '65W PPS' charger gave 53.16 W (60 W cable) and 54.53 W (100 W e-mark cable) in Super Fast Charging 3.0; a 100 W PD-only charger gave about 24 W
findings.source_title: Galaxy S26 Ultra Charging Speed: Wired and Wireless — All Modes Tested - Maplee-Tech
findings.note: Byline only 'Maplee-Tech', April 2026 (updated 2026-10-20). Chargers are unbranded, there is no method or meter, and the page is an Amazon affiliate. It backs up Techtest's figure for chargers without PPS, but it is weak on its own.
